notes: Reading gate discharged before any claim, in this session: AGENTS.md, docs/DESIGN-GATE.md §1 topic index, docs/architecture/actor-hud-ideal.md §4.1 and §5.1a, docs/contributing/live-probe-standard.md, the three prior reports in the branch worktree. The two §1 rows this work sits under are 'Anything a player sees (UI)' and 'Proving a feature works live / any debug call used as evidence' — the latter is the row that makes a response body insufficient as proof.

The overriding rule for this lane is the 2026-09-13 bound-loadout-hub incident: a probe fed fabricated state into the Injector and read it back from the SAME injector's telemetry, returning ok:true for a feature that was broken until a human looked at the real game screen. So this lane keeps three things apart: (a) the Server answers the route with JSON, (b) the page's own fetch path receives JSON with non-null hudGlyph, (c) a glyph is DRAWN and visible in a screenshot. (c) is the claim; (a) and (b) are not. All three were read separately and all three agree — but only (c) is reported as the finding.

The control that makes (b) mean anything is the SPA fallback, and it was MEASURED here, not cited: on this Server an unmapped path answers 200 text/html (403 bytes of the real index.html) for BOTH /api/... and /... paths, while the actor-surface route answers 200 application/json 24968B. Arm B of the browser probe does not hand-write that HTML — it fetches a real unmapped path and replays the server's own answer, so the offline arm is the genuine pre-fix shape.

RESULT: the glyphs render. With the route answering JSON, the page's boot query receives hudPresentation 36/30/4.5 and 6/7 non-null hudGlyph rows (versionStamp element:2), the derived /actor-hud-elements/*.png URLs answer 200 image/png, and the Phaser canvas identity row shows a larger orange flame and a smaller blue crystal in the screenshot. Blocking the route back to the SPA fallback on the same build removes both from the canvas and changes nothing else.

CORRECTION to the brief's premise, and it is worth more than the green: 'with no hudPresentation every glyph is skipped, so the fixture renders nothing' is TRUE on the Phaser canvas and FALSE on the React Inspector. ActorHudDisplay.ts:101-136 reads hudPresentation for its sizes; ActorHudInspector.tsx:50 uses a fixed Tailwind h-6 w-6 and never reads it, and the offline fixtureCatalog already imports element-catalog.v2.json directly (actorSurfaceCatalog.ts:16) so its rows carry hudGlyph. Measured: the two Inspector screenshots from the server-fed and fixture-fed arms are BYTE-IDENTICAL (sha256 80EDDC09...). So before the route existed the two HUD surfaces disagreed with each other; the route fix closed that disagreement, it did not rescue an Inspector that was never broken.

CAVEAT that matters more than the green: the glyph is NOT visible on the first board-stats even on a correct build. ensureElementTexture (ActorHudDisplay.ts:21-33) starts an async scene.load.image and then returns scene.textures.exists(key), which is still false on that call, so the draw site skips; nothing re-runs setHudDisplay until another snapshot arrives. Measured over five distinct board-stats: element0 false,false,TRUE,TRUE and element1 false,false,false,TRUE. The route fix is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT for a glyph to be on screen, and any single-event e2e assertion would read as a false red on a correct build.

omni (presentationOnly, no hudGlyph) — measured, NOT fixed, and not my call: clean skip on both surfaces. Canvas: identity/shield/status rows all present, the element slot simply absent, no crash, no ErrorBoundary. Inspector: imgCount=0, i.e. no is created at all (actorHudElementArt.ts:6 returns undefined before any URL is built), and the network log shows NO request for an omni art URL. Because ActorHudDisplay.ts:106 filters zero-width entries out of the layout array, the remaining identity items re-centre: the row is shorter and centred, not padded with a hole. The data belongs to the active session actor-hud-element-icons-20260917; deciding it needs tools/tuning/publish.py, never a hand edit.

Ports: this lane's Server listens on 5131 (FUSIONRPG_URLS; --urls and ASPNETCORE_URLS are ignored by this app, Program.cs:15-16) with FUSIONRPG_DATA pointed at a scratch dir outside the repo. :5088 and :5111 were never used and :5101 (the branch's own original worktree server) was left listening and untouched, measured before and after. The SPA was served BY the Server (wwwroot copied next to the exe) rather than by `vite preview`, because lib/bus/rest.ts:1-6 hardcodes DEV_API=http://127.0.0.1:5088 in dev and returns '' in a production build with no Vite proxy — so a preview-hosted page could never reach a real route, and a dev-hosted page would have hit the owner's forbidden port.

Board data was injected through the FE's own log-event hook window.__fusionRpgAppendLogEvent (log-store.ts:123) with board.start + debug.board-stats carrying the repo's own e2e/fixtures/actor-hud-golden.json shape plus the branch's elements field — the same path the shipped mocked spec e2e/actor-hud.spec.ts uses. So this lane proves the WEB RENDER PATH given a real board-shaped snapshot; it does NOT prove the Unity -> Server -> web ingest, and it does not re-assert the branch's own prior v7 live evidence.

One extra shell mock beyond e2e/helpers/mock-shell.ts was needed and is disclosed: /api/onboarding/*/first-open -> {opened:false}. The rift-gate entry-landing rule (useEntryLanding.ts:40-49 -> shouldLandOnSanctum) navigates to /sanctum and REPLACES the pinned route once the durable first-open fact is true — and on a deployed Server it genuinely is (measured {opened:true, openedUtc:2026-09-26T01:50:30Z}), so a pinned #/lawn is correctly overwritten and panel-lawn-inspector never appears. That is correct product behaviour, not a defect. /api/catalogs/actor-surface and /actor-hud-elements/* were NEVER mocked in the positive arm.

One measured wrinkle that cost a probe run and would cost a test author the same: debug.board-stats carries the WHOLE board, not a delta. Sending two occupants as two events leaves only the later one. Both must ride in one payload.

NOT PROVEN and stated as such: the Unity/in-game HUD (out of scope per the brief — FUSIONRPG_GAME_POOL is unset, the default install is shared, no injector deployed, no game launched or killed, and the Injector was not compiled because there is no game dir); the real board's re-drive cadence, so whether the first-frame skip of the note above is invisible in a real run is unmeasured; Firefox/WebKit/mobile (one Chromium, Playwright 1.62.1, one deviceScaleFactor); and the pre-existing reds the two prior lanes reported (Core.Expeditions.Tests 11/38, one Guard.Tests failure), which I neither confirmed nor contradicted and did not run.
